tools_ro_sha256_recorded_by: run.py provenance() at each run's 00_inputs.json (tools/iotrace/iotrace.c, tools/iotrace/README.md)
gate_order: PRE_GPU: verify.py --selftest, --seqtest, --preflight --run-id run01; RUN01_PRESENT: run.py --run-id run01 --execute, then verify.py --selftest, --seqtest, --between-runs --run01-id run01; RUN02_PRESENT: run.py --run-id run02 --execute, then verify.py --selftest, --seqtest, --captured --run01-id run01 --run02-id run02
gate_smoke: run.py's smoke_gate() runs a baseline_check same_cb case into work/<run-id>/, never raw/, and requires natural_chain_ok (and found_seg0/1/2) true before raw/<run-id>/ is created; a smoke failure is a pre-capture STOP with no raw/ directory left behind
gate_cross_run: run01 and run02's 02_results.jsonl (the GATED file) must be byte-identical per case (same case sequence, each case's JSON-decoded record equal) -- no GPU address, split-address link word, or location-dependent pointer field is ever present in that file (schema.py's whitelist construction + assert_no_address_leak, exercised by --selftest); raw addresses live only in the sibling 02_results_addrs.jsonl, which is NOT part of the cross-run gate and is expected to differ between runs
no_nondeterministic_field_in_gated_paylo: every gated field is either case identity, a structural boolean/count, a command-buffer status code, the link TAG byte alone (never its address-bearing hi/lo words), a deterministic tag-derived readback word (computed from our own fixed dispatch-order encoding, never from a captured address), or (codeswap only) a CDM record hex string with its own +0x08 location-dependent pointer field redacted to a fixed placeholder; verify.py --selftest proves this construction is invariant across two synthetic fixtures whose absolute addresses differ
fixtures_note: verify.py --selftest fixtures are literal reproductions of this experiment's own informal calibration observations (see PROGRESS.md): the 732/732/36 same_cb chain shape, tag 0x20, the skip_seg1 positive result's exact field values, and the codeswap kernel_x/kernel_y record pair's exact captured bytes -- not an invented shape
safety: one case per subprocess; 15s in-harness hardware watchdog (completion handler + timed dispatch_semaphore_wait, never a bare waitUntilCompleted) plus a 40s process-level timeout in run.py; cases ordered by increasing risk per casematrix.py; a fault or hang is a recorded result, never silently retried or dropped; a process-level timeout that would indicate the in-harness watchdog itself failed to return is grounds to STOP the whole run and report BLOCKED, not to continue the matrix
